rules.sentence: Anterior interosseous nerve syndrome presents as a rare motor neuropathy involving the flexor pollicis longus, the radial portion of the flexor digitorum profundus, and the pronator quadratus, without associated sensory loss.
Clinicians must distinguish true anterior interosseus nerve syndrome—often attributed to idiopathic immune-mediated neuritis—from isolated traumatic nerve injuries and local tendon pathologies.

Conservative management remains the initial approach; surgical exploration and decompression may follow after failed nonoperative treatment, particularly in cases involving identifiable compressive lesions.
